pillars.note: No pillar-specific statement. The objectives are smoke points and sooting of gas jet diffusion flames; the impact is 'to help design safer spacecraft environments', and the PSI SubResearch Area is 'Fire Safety'. Smoke production could relate to detection, but no cited line says so. Pillar list left empty on purpose; the reviewer should decide.

evidence.quote: (1) Identify the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames under various co-flow conditions in microgravity.
(3) Quantify the sooting propensity of different fuels, such as ethylene, propane, and propylene mixtures.
(1) Will improve our understanding of soot formation mechanisms and help design safer spacecraft environments.

hardware.value: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with a flow duct, integrated nozzles, cameras and a fuel delivery system, on the ISS

nominal_atmosphere.note: O2 only: the glovebox was flushed with ISS cabin air whose O2 mole fraction is maintained within 19 to 24 percent (p. 19). No pressure is set: the only pressure in the report is a calculation assumption (burner gas properties at 298 K and 101 kPa, p. 20), not a chamber condition. The experimental table has no O2 or pressure column.
